item.title: Weekly Newsletter #29 — June 10, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #29 · June 10, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🏛️ WE WENT TO HARRISBURG

Yesterday, we went to Harrisburg with the Bicycle Coalition, PA Safe Roads PAC, and Families for Safe Streets to show our support for safer streets for all.

🏘️ HOMES BELONG NEAR TRANSIT

Support more homes near transit!

Our city's vast transit network is an incredible asset--but restrictive zoning around transit stops prevents us from taking full advantage of it!

Homes near frequent transit provide valuable access to car-free transportation, but the areas around our transit stations are far too often filled with parking lots and drive-thrus.

Bill 260517 is a step in the right direction towards fixing this, but it only applies to 13 stations on the L.

City Council needs to pass this bill and follow it up with additional legislation adding stations on the B, T, Regional Rail, and our busiest bus corridors.

Read more in this piece in the Inquirer from our housing organizer, Jay Arzu: Philadelphia built a mass transit system. Now let people live next to it. | Opinion

🛠️ THE FIX FOR MORE PUBLIC SPACES

We love Philadelphia's public spaces.

But there's a little known barrier working against them: insurance costs.

The City requires that stewards of public spaces--parklets, streeteries, pedestrian plazas--hold insurance, and that they indemnify the city in the event of lawsuits.

This has high costs, and the evidence suggests it's not even needed!

Read more in the Philadelphia Citizen: Guest Commentary: The Insurance Trap Killing Our Public Spaces

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🗞️ 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

Inquirer.com / Philadelphia built a mass transit system. Now let people live next to it. | Opinion

The bill covers just 13 stations, all on the Market-Frankford Line. Most Philadelphians do not live near the El. I think about the family in the Northeast that cannot reach a steady job without a second car. I think about the retiree near Broad Street who cannot easily get to one of our region’s best hospitals. If the zoning change stops there, we will have passed a good policy and confined it to a footprint too small to reach them.

–5th Square Advocacy Housing Organizer Jay Arzu

The Philadelphia Citizen / Guest Commentary: A Dollar Won’t Do

The Mayor and City Council should reject the flat fee, accept the percentage-based structure, and advocate for a rate high enough to actually matter. The reason to get this right goes beyond this year’s school budget. Philadelphia, and every other American city, has a narrow window to establish sound rideshare tax policy before widespread autonomous vehicles make it politically much harder.

–5th Square Advocacy Treasurer Russell Richie

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏫 UNIVERSAL STUDENT FARES PETITION

Sign this petition to support expanding student transit cards to cover more students and provide transit access on evenings, weekends, and summers.

 

✍️ TRAIL SURVEY

Take this quick, 3-minute survey to help the Bicycle Coalition and Circuit Trails understand how you use trails throughout the region.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

📅 EVENTS

Jun 11

SW Philly Transit Accessibility Audit

5:00 PM to 7:00 PM · Cobbs Creek Library, 5800 Cobbs Creek Parkway

Join Transit Forward Philly for an accessibility audit of bus and trolley stops in SW Philly.
Jun 17

Policy Social and Celebration with BCGP and TFP

5:30 PM · Resurrection Philadelphia, 123 S 17th St

Join the Bicycle Coalition and Transit Forward Philly to celebrate wins in bike advocacy, Circuit Trails, transit, and pedestrian safety! BCGP Policy Director Julio Rodriguez will share policy priorities for 2026, and attendees will discuss ideas for the coming year.
Jun 27

Biking with Toddlers 101 Webinar

1:30 PM to 2:30 PM · Online Webinar

Learn how to safely bike with young children. This webinar will feature a presentation by two local doctors followed by a Q&A section.
Jun 28

Teddy Einstein Exit Party

2:00 PM to 8:00 PM · Clark Park

Celebrate the life of Teddy Einstein with life stations commemorating the different chapters of his life amidst food, drinks, and lawn games.
Aug 08

Philly Mayor's Cup

Belmont Plateau

The Philly Running Alliance is hosting a team race where runners compete for their chosen local running club, featuring races of varying length through historic West Fairmount Park.

🚌 TRANSIT

🚲 MOBILITY

  • GIS Program Lead

The Inquirer / Data & AI Enablement Architect

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #28 — June 2, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #28 · June 02, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🌇 TUESDAY OPEN STREETS

For the month of June, Center City District is bringing open streets to the Gayborhood on Tuesdays from 4:00-9:00 PM--and the first one is today!

 

🚲 ARAMINGO AVE SAFETY UPGRADES

We recently asked for your help in calling on PennDOT to make Aramingo Ave safer following the death of Glen Colville at the hands of a driver who plowed through flex posts into the bike lane.

At a meeting last week, PennDOT announced that it will replace flexposts with Toronto-style concrete barriers. While we wish it was done sooner, it's a great change that will hopefully prevent more families from losing loved ones.

Source: PBA

Thank you for signing the petition and thank you our partners at the Bicycle Coalition and PBA for supporting a safer Aramingo Ave.

💳 PUSH FOR UNIVERSAL STUDENT FARES BEFORE SUMMER

🏟️ THE SPORTS COMPLEX NEEDS MORE TRANSIT

At a time when SEPTA is still facing a long-term funding crisis, last week's announcement from Gov. Shapiro of $30 million in state funds for Stadium District roadways was a major disappointment.

The best way to reduce congestion is by investing in transit, not more road capacity. We need the support of the Commonwealth to make that happen.

See our full statement here.

👶 BIKING WITH TODDLERS

Our streets are for everyone and that includes toddlers!

Want to try biking with your young child, but unsure how to do it safely?

Join Philly Bike Action's webinar on June 27th. This one-hour webinar will discuss strategies for biking safely with young children, featuring a presentation by local doctors, and a Q&A section at the end. 

🔍 TRANSIT ACCESSIBILITY AUDIT

This Saturday, June 6th, join Transit Forward Philly for an accessibility audit of bus and L stops in Kensington.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🗞️ 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

The Inquirer / Gov. Shapiro announces almost $30 million highway investment for Philly stadium district

“Today’s announcement from Gov. Shapiro spending $30 million in state funds for Stadium District roadways is a major disappointment when SEPTA is still facing a long-term funding crisis threatening transit service,” transit advocacy group Fifth Square said in a statement Thursday. “The most effective way to manage congestion at the Stadium District is to encourage spectators to take SEPTA instead.”

Metro Philadelphia / Philly rolls out traffic safety signs amid string of deadly crashes

“In a collision at 25 miles per hour, pedestrians have a 90% chance of surviving,” Miles Owen, of 5th Square, said at a news conference Monday morning. “That percentage drastically decreases as the speed goes up. This sign makes that visible and reinforces the stakes.”

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏫 UNIVERSAL STUDENT FARES PETITION

Sign this petition to support expanding student transit cards to cover more students and provide transit access on evenings, weekends, and summers.

 

✍️ TRAIL SURVEY

Take this quick, 3-minute survey to help the Bicycle Coalition and Circuit Trails understand how you use trails throughout the region.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

📅 EVENTS

Jun 03

Transit for All PA Harrisburg Day of Action

9:30 AM to 3:30 PM · PA Capitol Building / Travel from 30th St Station

Transit systems all across the Commonwealth are facing dire funding shortfalls--join transit riders and workers from across PA in Harrisburg to demand action from our legislators.
Jun 04

Statewide Active Transportation Summit

8:30 AM to 4:30 PM · Harrisburg: 212 Locust St

Pennsylvanians from across the state working on improving walking, biking, and accessibility will gather in Harrisburg to meet others doing this work in their communities, see examples of work underway, and discover key elements to help you bring active transportation improvements home for your area.
Jun 06

Belmont Water Treatment Plant Open House

10:00 AM to 2:00 PM · Belmont Water Treatment Plant, 4300 W Ford Rd

The Philadelphia Water Department is welcoming the public for tours of a drinking water treatment plant. Come see how PWD keeps your tap water safe to drink and use every day.
Jun 06

Kensington Transit Accessibility Audit

11:00 AM to 1:00 PM · Harrowgate Park, 3455 Kensington Ave

Join Transit Forward Philadelphia for accessibility audit of bus and L stops in Kensington.
Jun 09

Bridging Blocks | Streets for Everyone: Bikes, Cars, and Pedestrian Rights

5:30 PM to 7:30 PM · Parkway Central Library, 4FL Skyline Room

Join WHYY for a community conversation discussing the safety of people walking and biking in Philadelphia and what city leaders, decision-makers, and advocates can do to improve safety.
Jun 27

Biking with Toddlers 101 Webinar

1:30 PM to 2:30 PM · Online Webinar

Learn how to safely bike with young children. This webinar will feature a presentation by two local doctors followed by a Q&A section.
Aug 08

Philly Mayor's Cup

Belmont Plateau

The Philly Running Alliance is hosting a team race where runners compete for their chosen local running club, featuring races of varying length through historic West Fairmount Park.

The New York Times / How to Stop the Affluent From Rigging the Housing Market

🚌 TRANSIT

Inquirer.com / A former SEPTA trolley driver is now tasked with saving the region’s transit system. Can Scott Sauer do it?

Audacy / Biking advocates demand safety improvements at deadly Port Richmond intersection

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #27 — May 26, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #27 · May 26, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🏘️ MORE HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Help us push for more homes near transit!

Philadelphia faces interconnected crises: rising housing costs, skyrocketing gas prices, worsening traffic, and a SEPTA budget shortfall. There's a $0 solution — Transit-Oriented Communities (TOC) legislation.

Mayor Parker's proposed TOC bills would allow more housing near transit, boosting SEPTA ridership and helping more residents put down roots in the city.

However the current legislation falls short: only 13 L stations are included (0 B stations!), and parking mandates near transit remain in place.

Support stronger legislation with:

  • Full removal of parking mandates near transit
  • Coverage expanded to the Broad Street Line, Regional Rail, and trolleys
  • A ½-mile radius around each transit stop
  • By-right multifamily housing in residential districts near transit

🕯️ RESCHEDULED: RIDE OF SILENCE TOMORROW

Due to last Wednesday's heavy rain, the annual Ride of Silence has been rescheduled for tomorrow, Wednesday, May 27th.

To honor the bicyclists killed or injured on our streets over the past year, we'll ride together in complete silence.

The ride will leave from City Hall, traveling 8 miles at a slow, casual pace to the Art Museum for a brief memorial bike lift.

2026 Ride of Silence
RESCHEDULED: Tomorrow, Wednesday, May 27th, 6:45 PM
North Apron of City Hall to Art Museum Steps

📣 SUPPORT THE CIRCUIT TRAILS

The Circuit Trails needs your help!

Under the current presidential administration, federal funding for bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure is rapidly drying up.

You can help by sending a letter to officials, asking them to support continued investment, maintenance and expansion of the Circuit trails across the region to ensure they remain safe and accessible for all.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🗞️ 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

The Philadelphia Tribune / Opposition builds against school district's fare evasion program

“If we truly want our students in classrooms and participating in extracurricular activities, we must create systems that help them get there safely and consistently,” said Alex Milone, transit committee co-chair for 5th Square Advocacy, in a statement.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

Weekly Newsletter #25 · May 13, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

📚 TOMORROW: LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

It's finally here: our book talk event with Life After Cars authors Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon is tomorrow night!

Life After Cars Book Event
with Sarah Goodyear & Doug Gordon from The War on Cars Podcast
TOMORROW, THURSDAY, May 14th at 7 PM
Resurrection Philadelphia, 17th & Sansom Streets

Get Your Ticket Today

 
The event will be kicked off by safe-streets champion, State Senator Nikil Saval, with Inquirer architecture critic Inga Saffron as emcee. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.

Get Your Ticket Today

🕯️ RIDE OF SILENCE NEXT WEEK

Next week on Wednesday, May 20th, join us for the Ride of Silence.

To honor the bicyclists killed or injured on our streets over the past year, we'll ride together in complete silence.

The ride will leave from City Hall, traveling 8 miles at a slow, casual pace to the Art Museum for a brief memorial bike lift.

2026 Ride of Silence
Wednesday, May 20th, 6:45 PM
North Apron of City Hall to Art Museum Steps

🚘 SAFER STREETS... FOR DRIVERS

Our streets are getting safer... for some road users.

An analysis by Philly Bike Action found that while overall fatal crashes decreased last year, crashes with serious injuries were up for non-motorists! This means more pedestrians and micromobility riders were getting hit and seriously injured by drivers.

Any reduction in deaths on our streets is a step in the right direction, but we can't leave vulnerable road users behind. We need streets that are safe for all, not just those behind the wheel.

Here are three actions you can take to help make that happen:

  1. Tell PennDOT to make Aramingo Ave safer
  2. Support legalizing parking protected bike lanes
  3. Sign up to volunteer with out Vision Zero committee

Weekly Newsletter #25 · May 13, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

📚 TOMORROW: LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

It's finally here: our book talk event with Life After Cars authors Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon is tomorrow night!

Life After Cars Book Event
with Sarah Goodyear & Doug Gordon from The War on Cars Podcast
TOMORROW, THURSDAY, May 14th at 7 PM
Resurrection Philadelphia, 17th & Sansom Streets

Get Your Ticket Today

 
The event will be kicked off by safe-streets champion, State Senator Nikil Saval, with Inquirer architecture critic Inga Saffron as emcee. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.

Get Your Ticket Today

🕯️ RIDE OF SILENCE NEXT WEEK

Next week on Wednesday, May 20th, join us for the Ride of Silence.

To honor the bicyclists killed or injured on our streets over the past year, we'll ride together in complete silence.

The ride will leave from City Hall, traveling 8 miles at a slow, casual pace to the Art Museum for a brief memorial bike lift.

2026 Ride of Silence
Wednesday, May 20th, 6:45 PM
North Apron of City Hall to Art Museum Steps

🚘 SAFER STREETS... FOR DRIVERS

Our streets are getting safer... for some road users.

An analysis by Philly Bike Action found that while overall fatal crashes decreased last year, crashes with serious injuries were up for non-motorists! This means more pedestrians and micromobility riders were getting hit and seriously injured by drivers.

Any reduction in deaths on our streets is a step in the right direction, but we can't leave vulnerable road users behind. We need streets that are safe for all, not just those behind the wheel.

Here are three actions you can take to help make that happen:

  1. Tell PennDOT to make Aramingo Ave safer
  2. Support legalizing parking protected bike lanes
  3. Sign up to volunteer with out Vision Zero committee
